_comments: Seeds Hierarchy.IsHierarchy=true in EntityField.Configuration for FormCategory.ParentID.
Form categories are a genuine tree: the builder nests them and scripts/pg-objectmodel-test.mjs
asserts vwFormCategories.RootParentID walks to the root. MJ 6.1.0-edge.3 gated the base-view
hierarchy columns behind this flag, so without this file CodeGen drops RootParentID and every
read of the entity fails with 'Invalid column name' — which a grid renders as 'no data'. #156.
BOTH RECORDS IN THIS FILE: no `uuidgen` primaryKey UUID anywhere here, departing from CLAUDE.md's
convention on purpose. Every id in this file is an @lookup because these are UPDATEs to Entity /
EntityField rows CodeGen created, whose ids differ per host — there is no id of ours to declare. The
consequence is that check-release-seed-coverage.mjs, which collects only UUID-shaped ids, measures
nothing for these two records; that is correct, not a gap.
BOTH RECORDS IN THIS FILE, second point: on why they key on the entity NAME while V202609050300 keys
on SchemaName + BaseTable, which its own comment calls the safe key — both are right for where they
run. mj sync's @lookup has no SchemaName+BaseTable form, and this file is pushed against OUR database,
where the MJ_BizApps_Forms: prefix is what mj.config.cjs sets. The migration is the artifact that reaches
other hosts, where that prefix is configurable — so it cannot use the name.
Seeds Hierarchy.IsHierarchy=FALSE for Form.TemplateSourceFormID — a deliberate negative,
recorded rather than left ambiguous (the bizapps-tasks precedent for Tasks.ParentID).
V202608211600's header states the link is set on the TEMPLATE row, points at the form it was
saved FROM, and is deliberately never set on forms created from a template. It is a one-hop
provenance pointer, not a tree — the MergedIntoID / PreviousVersionID class MJ's hierarchy
guide names as exactly what the gate suppresses. Seeding true would put a recursive-CTE OUTER
APPLY on vwForms, the view every form load reads, to answer a question that never chains. #156.
